first_impression: Looks like a charming, low-poly pastoral puzzle game that actually understands sheepdog mechanics instead of just using them as a skin. The visual presentation is clean and cozy, reminiscent of Untitled Goose Game meets a rustic arcade sim. It looks tight and focused, though 9 levels feels pretty short for a ten-dollar purchase.
best_things: The range ring and dashed influence circle immediately communicate herding radius and pressure without muddying the field.
The scenario variety across the 9 evenings introduces genuine rule tweaks like stubborn rams, lambs following ewes, and the formal sheepdog trial course.
The UI typography and briefing cards have an authentic, polished editorial feel that sells the Highland farm theme.

worst_problems.problem: The total campaign is only 9 short evenings, which looks like it would take less than 45 minutes to finish completely.
worst_problems.suggestion: Double the level count or include procedural/endless seasonal variations with leaderboards so there is actual meat on the bones.

worst_problems.problem: Night Watch survival mode looks visually flat and hard to read, with wolves and sheep barely contrasting against dark navy ground.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add rim lighting or eye-shine for the wolves and glowing silhouettes for sheep so defending them doesn't strain your eyes.

worst_problems.problem: The charm upgrades feel extremely passive and minor (+8% speed, 30% stamina) rather than changing how you actually pilot Pip.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give charms active perks like flanking whistle commands or quick sharp turns instead of standard percentage stat bumps.

worst_problems.problem: The dog model in motion looks stiff and board-flat in top-down views, lacking the fluid low-slung stalking animation of a real border collie.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give Pip more squash-and-stretch and a noticeable crouched stalking run animation when creeping.

worst_problems.problem: The minimap styling looks like an unfinished placeholder vector drawing compared to the stylized 3D terrain.
worst_problems.suggestion: Render the minimap as a hand-drawn parchment survey map with rustic ink outlines and watercolor fills.

boredom_points: Waiting for slow-moving sheep to cross narrow gates or bridges when you have already aligned them perfectly.
Replaying earlier levels just to grind stars for the 13-star charm unlock when there are only 9 total stages.
confusions: In evening-5-trial.jpg, how strictly the judges track line deviation between the obstacle gates versus just passing through the posts.
Whether wolves can attack Pip directly or if they only target stray sheep.
wish_list: A full traditional sheepdog trials mode with authentic whistle audio commands.
More weather effects that affect terrain friction like slick mud or deep drifts of snow.
Steam Workshop support or a level editor to design community trial courses.
one_line_review: Short but sweet Highland herding sim that captures the tense geometry of sheepdog work, though it runs out of pasture far too quickly.
